heading: Grounded in academic research, proven across the globe.
lead: Ixmucané GeoPower pairs research training in computational geothermal reservoir engineering — from the University of Auckland's Geothermal Institute — with decades of hands-on reservoir engineering experience across geothermal fields worldwide, from the Americas to Africa, Asia, Europe and the Pacific.

people.name: Michael O'Sullivan
people.affiliation: Professor of Engineering Science, University of Auckland
people.bio: One of the world's leading experts in geothermal reservoir modelling; recipient of the Henry J. Ramey Award for Geothermal Reservoir Engineering (2011) and Fellow of the Institution of Professional Engineers New Zealand. PhD in Applied Mechanics (Caltech), with over 45 years at the University of Auckland (1969–2015) plus visiting positions at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory and New York University. Developed core numerical modelling techniques used across geothermal fields in New Zealand and internationally.

people.name: John O'Sullivan
people.affiliation: Associate Professor & Co-Director, Geothermal Institute, University of Auckland
people.bio: PhD in Engineering Science (Auckland), MS in Aeronautics and Astronautics (Stanford), BE with First Class Honours (Auckland). Works globally with geothermal industry stakeholders on resource assessment, advanced simulator technology, cloud computing and uncertainty quantification, supercritical resources and digital-twin development — leading training programmes across Asia, South America, Africa, Europe and Australia, and collaborating with Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory and the US Department of Energy.

people.name: Enrique Porras Mendieta
people.affiliation: Independent Geothermal Consultant — formerly Principal Reservoir Engineer, ORMAT Inc., and Field Manager, Momotombo Geothermal Complex, Nicaragua
people.bio: PhD in Engineering from Kyushu University (2005). Nearly four decades in the industry — from Nicaragua's ENEL to three decades at ORMAT, most recently as Principal Reservoir Engineer, before going independent in 2025 — building and calibrating numerical models for Momotombo, Zunil, Amatitlán, Olkaria III and Dixie Valley, and designing the downhole pressure-monitoring and calcite-inhibition systems now running at several of those fields. Co-author, with Julian Xicara, of the 2020 World Geothermal Congress paper on a new numerical model of the Amatitlán system, and of three Geothermal Resources Council papers (2021–2025) on calcite inhibition and injection-well caustic treatments at Zunil, Guatemala.

people.name: Michael Gravatt
people.affiliation: Senior Lecturer, Geothermal Institute, University of Auckland
people.bio: PhD and BE (First Class Honours) in Engineering Science, University of Auckland. Since 2019 has worked to standardise geothermal modelling approaches and make the technology accessible to industry and students — the same modelling framework this consultancy builds on. Research spans geothermal resource assessment, critical mineral extraction, CO2 sequestration, supercritical resources and digital twins, with industry collaborations including Contact Energy, Pertamina Geothermal Energy and Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory.

people.name: Ryan Tonkin
people.affiliation: Research Fellow, Geothermal Institute, University of Auckland
people.bio: PhD and BE with First Class Honours in Engineering Science, University of Auckland (2021). Research Fellow developing transient wellbore simulators that model complex two-phase flow inside geothermal wells — the same class of tool behind our own ESP/GBOP pump-sizing work — with further research in wellbore-reservoir coupling, supercritical flow and CO2 sequestration. Lectures for the Faculty of Engineering, teaches Geothermal Institute short courses on reservoir modelling and resource estimation, and consults for geothermal companies internationally.

people.name: Ken Dekkers
people.affiliation: Research Engineer, Geothermal Institute, University of Auckland
people.bio: Master's (2021) and Bachelor's (2017) in Mechanical Engineering from Eindhoven University of Technology — his master's thesis, on inverse modelling and uncertainty quantification of an updated Rotorua geothermal model, was itself a collaboration with the University of Auckland. Research Engineer at the Geothermal Institute since 2020, now maintaining the cloud computing infrastructure behind fast, parallel Waiwera reservoir simulations and developing a general-purpose uncertainty-quantification framework used across the group's modelling projects, including a new method for greenfield resource assessment that combines field data with expert knowledge to constrain the model ensemble.

people.name: Julian Xicara
people.affiliation: Doctoral Candidate, Geothermal Institute, University of Auckland
people.bio: Started in geothermal in 2006 at a binary power plant in Guatemala, followed by specialised geothermal training in El Salvador (2012). Worked as a testing engineer for Ormat evaluating wells across multiple continents, then as an Ormat Resource Engineer in Nevada, and most recently as Senior Reservoir Engineer at Cyrq Energy. Holds an MSc with First Class Honours from the University of Auckland (thesis on the Amatitlán geothermal system) and is now a PhD candidate integrating geochemical data into resource assessment and uncertainty-quantification frameworks, across projects in Guatemala and the United States.
